claims.text: A controlled increase in Cr content promotes formation of a finely dispersed Laves phase.
The Cr-induced Laves phase is Cr2Ta.
The Laves phase increases local lattice distortion.
The Cr-induced Laves phase refines the grains.
The fine Laves phase provides heterogeneous nucleation sites for a dense protective oxide film.
Cr addition creates local compositional fluctuations that favor Laves-phase precipitation.
The Laves phase impedes dislocation motion.
CrTaO4, Cr2O3, and TiO2 are stable oxide species nucleated during high-temperature exposure.
Solid-solution and grain-boundary strengthening increase the alloy's mechanical strength.
The resulting protective oxide film reduces high-temperature oxidation attack.
The resulting protective oxide film reduces corrosion attack in NaCl solution.
The proposed Cr-induced modification does not significantly compromise the alloy's low density.
The initial lightweight alloy is a homogeneous BCC solid solution.
Rapid solidification during laser cladding promotes a fine, network-distributed Laves precipitate.
The Cr-modified alloy will have greater hardness than the Cr-free baseline.
The Cr-modified alloy will have lower oxide weight gain than the Cr-free baseline after high-temperature oxidation.
The Cr-modified alloy will have a lower corrosion rate than the Cr-free baseline in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
Excessive Cr causes over-precipitation of brittle intermetallics and consequent embrittlement or loss of ductility.
An oxidation test at 800 °C for 50 hours is proposed.
Corrosion testing in 3.5 wt% NaCl with Tafel analysis is proposed.

contradictions.description: Excessive Cr is defined as a condition under which the hypothesis should cease to hold, but embrittlement from excessive Cr is also presented as a result that falsifies the hypothesis. A result outside the stated validity range should not by itself falsify the bounded hypothesis.
The conditions call for potentiodynamic corrosion analysis, whereas the experimental design calls it potentiostatic measurement; these are distinct electrochemical methods.
The baseline is described as lacking targeted Cr addition, which does not necessarily mean zero Cr, while the experimental control is explicitly described as Cr-free.
